analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Out of control revisions
key_insights: October control group retail sales rose +0.6%, stronger than BofA's own above-consensus forecast.
August-September control group sales were revised up by a cumulative 70bp or more, which put the October control group level 1% above what consensus expected.
3Q spending is on track to be revised above 4% q/q saar, and 4Q looks stronger as well.
BofA's 4Q GDP tracking estimate is 2.4% q/q saar, up a tenth from its official forecast of 2.3%, after retail sales, industrial production, business inventories and import/export price data.
Today's events are FOMC minutes (2:00 PM), housing data, and remarks from Fed officials Daly, Barr, Williams and Kashkari.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above BofA's above-consensus forecast. Control group sales read into GDP, so the beat supports consumer spending estimates.
Raised the level of October control group sales to 1% above consensus expectations.
BofA expects 3Q spending to be revised above 4% q/q saar.
Up a tenth from BofA's official forecast of 2.3%. Tracking is a mechanical aggregation of incoming data, separate from the official forecast.
